title: Treelabeling
statementMd:
Eikooc and Sushi play a game.

The game is played on a tree having $n$ nodes numbered $1$ to $n$. Recall that a tree having $n$ nodes is an undirected, connected graph with $n-1$ edges.

They take turns alternately moving a token on the tree. **Eikooc makes the first move, placing the token** on any node of her choice. Sushi makes the next move, followed by Eikooc, followed by Sushi, and so on. In each turn after the first, a player must move the token to a node $u$ such that

- $u$ is adjacent to the node $v$ the token is currently on
- $u$ has not been visited before
- $u \oplus v \leq min(u, v)$

Here $x \oplus y$ denotes the [bitwise XOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitwise_operation#XOR) operation on integers $x$ and $y$.

Both the players play optimally. The player who is unable to make a move loses.

The following are examples which demonstrate the rules of the game.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3295a7d6e7a175749cce0ef394201d059dcccbfd.png) *Suppose Eikooc starts the game by placing the token at node $4$. Sushi then moves the token to node $6$, which is unvisited and adjacent to $4$. It also holds that $6 \oplus 4 = 2 \leq min(6, 4)$. In the next turn, Eikooc moves the token to node $5$, which is unvisited and adjacent to $6$. It holds that $5 \oplus 6 = 3 \leq min(5, 6)$. Sushi has no more moves to play, so she loses.* ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a67b0033a1f799229927f151e8e6cda92aa46b14.png) *Suppose Eikooc starts the game by placing the token at node $3$. Sushi moves the token to node $2$, which is unvisited and adjacent to $3$. It also holds that $3 \oplus 2 = 1 \leq min(3, 2)$. Eikooc cannot move the token to node $6$ since $6 \oplus 2 = 4 \nleq min(6, 2)$. Since Eikooc has no moves to play, she loses.*

Before the game begins, Eikooc decides to sneakily relabel the nodes of the tree in her favour. Formally, a relabeling is a permutation $p$ of length $n$ (sequence of $n$ integers wherein each integer from $1$ to $n$ occurs exactly once) where $p_i$ denotes the new numbering of node $i$.

She wants to maximize the number of nodes she can choose in the first turn which will guarantee her a win. Help Eikooc find any relabeling which will help her do so.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $t~(1 \le t \le 10^5)$  — the number of test cases. The description of each test case is as follows.

The first line of each test case contains an integer $n~(1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$  — the number of nodes in the tree.

The next $n-1$ lines contain two integers $u$ and $v$ $(1 \le u, v \le n; u \neq v)$  — denoting an edge between nodes $u$ and $v$.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case print any suitable relabeling  — a permutation of length $n$ which maximizes the number of nodes that can be chosen in the first turn that guarantee a win for Eikooc. If there are multiple such relabelings, you may print any of them.

## Note

In the first test case, Eikooc has only one choice. Sushi will have no moves to play after Eikooc chooses this node and Eikooc will win.

In the second test case, $1 \oplus 2 = 3 \nleq min(1, 2)$. Hence, after Eikooc picks either of the nodes, Sushi will have no moves to play and Eikooc will win. Both $\{1, 2\}$ and $\{2, 1\}$ are optimal relabelings.
statementZhMd:
Eikooc 和 Sushi 正在玩一个游戏。

游戏在一棵有 $n$ 个节点的树上进行，节点编号为 $1$ 到 $n$。回顾一下，有 $n$ 个节点的树是一个无向连通图，且恰有 $n-1$ 条边。

她们轮流在树上移动一个棋子。**Eikooc 先手，将棋子放置在她选择的任意节点上**。接下来由 Sushi 移动，然后是 Eikooc，再然后是 Sushi，如此交替进行。在第一次操作之后的每个回合中，玩家必须将棋子移动到节点 $u$，并满足：

- $u$ 与棋子当前所在的节点 $v$ 相邻；
- $u$ 之前未被访问过；
- $u \oplus v \leq min(u, v)$。

其中，$x \oplus y$ 表示整数 $x$ 和 $y$ 的[按位异或](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitwise_operation#XOR)运算。

双方都会采取最优策略。无法进行移动的玩家输掉游戏。

下面的例子展示了游戏规则。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3295a7d6e7a175749cce0ef394201d059dcccbfd.png) *假设 Eikooc 在游戏开始时将棋子放置在节点 $4$。随后 Sushi 将棋子移动到节点 $6$，节点 $6$ 未被访问过且与节点 $4$ 相邻。同时，$6 \oplus 4 = 2 \leq min(6, 4)$ 也成立。在下一回合中，Eikooc 将棋子移动到节点 $5$，节点 $5$ 未被访问过且与节点 $6$ 相邻。并且 $5 \oplus 6 = 3 \leq min(5, 6)$。Sushi 再也无法进行移动，因此她输掉了游戏。* ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a67b0033a1f799229927f151e8e6cda92aa46b14.png) *假设 Eikooc 在游戏开始时将棋子放置在节点 $3$。Sushi 将棋子移动到节点 $2$，节点 $2$ 未被访问过且与节点 $3$ 相邻。同时，$3 \oplus 2 = 1 \leq min(3, 2)$。Eikooc 无法将棋子移动到节点 $6$，因为 $6 \oplus 2 = 4 \nleq min(6, 2)$。由于 Eikooc 无法进行移动，她输掉了游戏。*

在游戏开始前，Eikooc 决定偷偷地对树上的节点重新编号，以便为自己谋取优势。形式化地说，重标号是一个长度为 $n$ 的排列 $p$（由 $n$ 个整数组成的序列，其中 $1$ 到 $n$ 的每个整数恰好出现一次），其中 $p_i$ 表示节点 $i$ 的新编号。

她希望最大化第一回合中她可以选择、且能够保证自己获胜的节点数量。请帮助 Eikooc 找到任意一种能够实现这一目标的重标号方案。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $t~(1 \leq t \leq 10^5)$ —— 测试用例的数量。每个测试用例的描述如下。

每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $n~(1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5)$ —— 树中节点的数量。

接下来的 $n-1$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $u$ 和 $v$ $(1 \leq u, v \leq n; u \neq v)$，表示节点 $u$ 和节点 $v$ 之间存在一条边。

保证所有测试用例的 $n$ 之和不超过 $2 \cdot 10^5$。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，输出任意一种合适的重标号方案——一个长度为 $n$ 的排列，使得第一回合中能够保证 Eikooc 获胜的可选节点数量最大。如果存在多个这样的重标号方案，可以输出其中任意一种。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，Eikooc 只有一种选择。在 Eikooc 选择该节点后，Sushi 将无法进行移动，因此 Eikooc 获胜。

在第二个测试用例中，$1 \oplus 2 = 3 \nleq min(1, 2)$。因此，在 Eikooc 选择任意一个节点后，Sushi 都将无法进行移动，Eikooc 获胜。${1, 2}$ 和 ${2, 1}$ 都是最优的重标号方案。
